construct: During antidiuresis, vasopressin increases urea permeability in the terminal inner medullary collecting duct through UT-A1 and related UT-A transporters. Reabsorbed urea accumulates in the inner medullary interstitium and recycles through thin limbs and medullary vessels, helping maintain the high medullary osmolality required for maximal water reabsorption and urine concentration.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Selective UT-A1 blockade with intact vasopressin and AQP2 reduces inner-medullary urea accumulation/recycling, weakens the medullary osmotic gradient, and lowers maximal urine osmolality.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Reduced thick-ascending-limb NaCl transport would also impair the medullary gradient, but the stem explicitly states sodium transport is unaffected.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The intervention is isolated to UT-A1, so reduced medullary urea accumulation is the unique causal change.
